traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION are satisfied: - Core Functionality: The valid-req-reference rule reads referenced story files, extracts REQ- IDs, and verifies that each @req matches an existing requirement. Missing IDs produce a specific reqMissing diagnostic. - Quality Standards: Validation is content-based and format-agnostic, using a regex that supports multiple requirement formats (plain lines, bullet lists, and across sections). Tests include both standard story files and a bullet-list fixture to prove robustness against different structures. - Integration: The rule reuses existing comment-based annotation parsing patterns, integrates with ESLint’s Program visitor lifecycle, and is registered and enabled in the plugin’s recommended/strict configs. - User Experience: Error messages are clear and contextual (include both reqId and storyPath for missing requirements, and storyPath for invalid paths). This aligns with the 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING story’s conventions. - Error Handling: Story-file reading is wrapped in try/catch; failures result in an empty requirement set rather than crashes. Path traversal and absolute paths are explicitly rejected with invalidPath diagnostics. This ensures graceful behavior when files are malformed, missing, or inaccessible. - Documentation: docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md and README.md document the behavior, link back to this story, and provide concrete examples of supported and failing cases. Together with comprehensive unit tests in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts, this confirms the story is fully implemented and working as specified.
